# Demo Manuscript

Smith and Jones report that participants "preferred the assisted workflow in every measured dimension" (Smith, 2023). Doe (2021) proposes a validated preference scale. Earlier foundations were laid by Kim (2019).

A fabricated work claims the opposite (Ghost et al., 2024).

One altered quote: participants "strongly preferred the assisted workflow in every dimension measured" (Smith, 2023). One fabricated quote: the scale "was rejected as fundamentally unreliable" (Doe, 2021).

This paragraph exists only to push the next quotation far enough away from the nearest citation above it. It restates, in plain prose with no quotation marks and no citation of its own, that the audit tool measures the distance in characters between every extracted quotation and the nearest in-text citation, and that when that distance exceeds the configured adjacency window the quotation is reported as unattributed rather than checked against any particular source, because attributing it to the wrong paper would be worse than not checking it at all. Padding text of this kind is unusual in a real manuscript, but it is exactly what this fixture needs in order to demonstrate the seventh finding type on its own, deterministically, without ever touching the adjacency threshold itself. A few more sentences keep the gap comfortably past the window so the test does not become fragile if the wording above is ever edited slightly.

"this rather long quotation has no citation attached to it at all"
